summary: P95/P99 latency spikes and request timeouts for text-generation (continuous batching suspected)
description: Issue summary: Over the last 6 hours Craftly AI has reported periodic p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional request timeouts (HTTP 504) for text-generation calls to the hosted API. Spikes are most pronounced for short prompts and low sustained QPS. Impact: customer-facing production traffic experiencing degraded response times and retries, elevated costs due to backoff/retries, and two customer timeouts observed in the last hour. Environment: prod, us-east-1. Recent changes: a scheduler tuning PR that adjusted continuous-batching parameters was rolled out to the serving-runtime on 2026-03-02. Hypothesis: batch-window/backpressure changes causing larger, infrequent batches under low QPS producing p99 tail and buffer timeouts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady low-QPS (0.5-2 qps) text-generation requests with short prompts to /v1/generate using redwood-v2-medium
2) Observe p95/p99 latency in API traces and sampling of streaming connections
3) Increase concurrency to simulate burst and observe that p50 remains stable while p95/p99 spike intermittently
4) Check serving runtime metrics (batch size distribution, batch_wait_ms histogram) during spikes
logs: Serving metrics snapshot (2026-03-03T09:40Z): batch_wait_ms p99=420ms, avg_batch_size=1.8, burst_batch_size=12
API gateway logs show 504s with upstream_connect_time ~500ms during spike windows
investigation_notes: 03-03 09:15 - Support triage: Customer provided request IDs and sample traces; p99 spikes correlate with elevated batch_wait_ms in serving runtime.
03-03 10:02 - Eng (Miguel) reproduced locally with load-tester using low qps and observed batch accumulation when target_batch_max_wait_ms was set to 200ms (previously 50ms).
03-03 10:30 - Correlation found to recent scheduler PR https://github.com/redwood/realtime-batching/pull/482 which increased default batch window to improve throughput for high QPS customers.

03-03 11:00 - Observed that under low QPS, larger windows increase tail latency because requests wait longer to form larger batches; streaming clients may hit application timeouts while waiting for token generation to start.
03-03 11:25 - Checked rollback history: change was toggled via feature flag ff/batching-window on 2026-03-02. Canary rollout expanded to 50% of serving fleet on 2026-03-02 22:00Z.
03-03 12:05 - Temporary mitigation tested: set ff/batching-window to 'low-latency' policy for the affected us-east capacity pool -> immediate reduction in p99 to ~85ms in test harness.

2) Roll forward fix to us-east and eu-west with canary, monitor batch_wait_ms and tail latency
3) Add automated rollback and alerting for batch_wait_ms p95>200ms
4) Follow up with customer (Craftly AI) on timeline and provide post-deployment verification
